home.about: I'm a BTS Cloud Computing student specializing in Linux server administration, networking, security, project management and web development.
home.development: Over time I have learned that organisation and planning are essential. Building on stable, well founded projects matters, because without a solid foundation it simply is not possible. I also learned not to limit myself to only what is asked of me, but to look beyond the task at hand. When working with a piece of software it is important to keep learning more about it and to actually test things myself. One lesson stands out in particular: not letting AI do everything, since that leads to losing track of the bigger picture and ultimately to not really knowing your own projects anymore. AI should always be used hand in hand with your own work, not as a replacement for it.

projects.title: LME
projects.subtitle: Luxembourg Media Engineering
projects.summary: An ambitious school entrepreneurship project that we're transforming into a real business.
projects.body: ## Project Overview **LME** (lme.lu) is an ambitious school entrepreneurship project that we're transforming into a real business. What started as an academic initiative is now evolving into a full-fledged startup, combining our learning experience with real-world business development. LME provides a **Secure Multi-Tenant Hosting Platform** built on Hetzner infrastructure, designed to offer small organizations and individual clients reliable web hosting without the complexity and cost of large cloud providers. ## Technology Stack ### Infrastructure & Virtualization - **Hetzner Dedicated Server** - Reliable German infrastructure provider - **Proxmox** - Enterprise-grade virtualization platform for VM management - **Docker + Docker Compose** - Container orchestration for service isolation ### Web Services & Security - **Nginx** - High-performance web server and reverse proxy - **Cloudflare** - DNS management, DDoS protection, and security features - **SSH & Firewall** - Secure access and network protection ### Monitoring & Management - **Raspberry Pi** - Independent external monitoring system - **Hetzner API** - Resource monitoring and server management - **Custom Scripts** - Automated availability checks and alerts ## Technical Architecture - **VM-Level Separation** - Each client website runs in a dedicated Proxmox virtual machine - **Container Isolation** - Docker Compose separates services within each VM - **Network Segmentation** - Firewall rules prevent cross-tenant access - **Security Measures** - SSH key-based authentication, automated updates, regular backups ## Business Development LME represents a unique combination of academic learning and real-world entrepreneurship: - **Project Management Course** - Developed for the Talent Exhibition as part of our school curriculum - **House of Entrepreneurship Partnership** - Guidance from Luxembourg's entrepreneurship ecosystem - **Team of Three** - Collaborative approach combining technical expertise and business development - **Market Focus** - Targeting small organizations who need reliable hosting without complexity

projects.title: LuxRP
projects.body: ## Project Overview LuxRP is a Luxembourg-based FiveM roleplay server that provides an immersive Grand Theft Auto V multiplayer experience. FiveM is a modification framework for GTA V, enabling players to engage in custom multiplayer experiences on dedicated servers with unique gameplay mechanics and community-driven roleplay scenarios. ## Technology Stack - **FiveM** - Multiplayer modification framework for GTA V built on CitizenFX - **NUI (New UI)** - HTML-based user interface system using Chromium Embedded Framework - **HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript** - Frontend development for in-game interfaces - **Lua** - Server scripting and game logic (handled by other team members) ## My Role I served as **Developer, Supporter, and Administrator**: ### Developer - **Custom UI Development** - Designed in-game interfaces using HTML, CSS, JavaScript within the FiveM NUI framework - **Responsive Design** - Created interfaces adapting to different screen resolutions - **Performance Optimization** - Ensured UIs were lightweight and performant ### Supporter & Administrator - **Conflict Resolution** - Managed support situations with diplomacy and fairness - **Player Assistance** - Helped with technical issues and rule clarifications - **Server Management** - Player management, policy enforcement, team coordination ## Featured Project: Funex **Funex** is a dual-platform communication system I developed that bridges web and in-game environments. It operates both as a standalone website and as an integrated in-game phone application. ### Technical Implementation - **Tech Stack** - HTML, CSS, JavaScript, PHP, MySQL, AJAX - **Dual Environment** - Works as web app and in-game mobile phone interface - **Character Sync** - Automatic synchronization with game database - **Multi-Character Support** - Each player can have multiple roleplay characters

projects.title: Grading Dino
projects.body: ## Project Overview Grading Dino is a research and development project from our Project Management course, focused on creating a modern grade management system. The project emphasizes secure, scalable architecture using industry-standard technologies and best practices. This system enables professors to efficiently manage student grades through an intuitive interface while maintaining strict security standards and data integrity. ## Technology Stack ### Backend & Database - **Django 5.0** - Full-featured web framework with built-in admin panel, authentication, and security features - **PostgreSQL 16** - Production-ready database with full ACID compliance and concurrent write support - **Python 3.11** - Modern programming language with strong typing and excellent ecosystem ### Security - **Argon2 Password Hashing** - Winner of the Password Hashing Competition (2015), developed at University of Luxembourg - **Django Security Features** - Built-in CSRF, XSS, and SQL injection protection - **Server-Side Validation** - All logic and validation handled securely on the server ### Frontend - **Pico.css** - Minimalist CSS framework (~10KB) with semantic HTML styling - **Server-Side Rendering** - Django templates for security and simplicity ### Deployment - **Docker + Docker Compose** - Containerized architecture with single-command startup - **Production-Ready** - Isolated containers with consistent environment across deployments ## Key Features - **Admin Panel** - Complete grade management UI for professors without custom development - **Authentication & Authorization** - User roles and permissions out-of-the-box - **Automated Forms & Validation** - Django's form generation with server-side validation - **Data Integrity** - PostgreSQL ACID compliance ensures reliable grade storage - **Concurrent Operations** - Multiple professors can grade simultaneously - **Single Command Deployment** - Simple `docker compose up` to start the entire system ## Technical Approach The project follows Django's "batteries included" philosophy, leveraging built-in features for rapid, secure development. The architecture prioritizes: - **Convention over Configuration** - Reduced complexity through framework standards - **Security by Default** - Multiple layers of built-in protection - **Scalability** - Docker containerization enables easy horizontal scaling - **Academic Credibility** - Argon2's Luxembourg university origin strengthens technical justification ## Research Outcomes This research project successfully demonstrated how modern web frameworks and containerization technologies can create secure, maintainable grade management systems with minimal custom development. The choice of Argon2, developed at University of Luxembourg, provides both technical excellence and local academic significance.

projects.title: Private Photo Cloud
projects.subtitle: Self-hosted · Google & Apple independent
projects.summary: Self-hosted Google Photos alternative: Immich on a Raspberry Pi 4, storage on a Ugreen NAS, accessible from anywhere via Tailscale
projects.body:
## Overview

Self-hosted replacement for Google Photos and Apple iCloud. Photos live on a local NAS, **Immich** runs in Docker on a Raspberry Pi 4, and **Tailscale** makes it accessible from anywhere, with no subscription and no third party cloud.

## Hardware

- **Ugreen NAS DH2300 (2-Bay)**: 2× 4 TB in RAID 1
- **Raspberry Pi 4 (8 GB)**: Docker host

## How it works

The NAS doesn't support Docker, so storage and compute are split: the NAS share is mounted on the Pi, and Immich reads and writes photos directly to that mount. Tailscale connects all my devices in a private mesh network, with no port forwarding and no public IP needed.

## Software

- **Immich**: self-hosted photo management, automatic mobile backup, face recognition, Google Photos-like UI
- **Docker**: runs the full Immich stack (server, ML, database, Redis)
- **Tailscale**: WireGuard-based VPN for secure remote access

projects.title: Server Virtualization Systems
projects.subtitle: VIRCL: BTS Cloud Computing
projects.summary: Proxmox VE & VMware ESXi: hypervisor setup, VM management, live migration and High Availability, VIRCL module
projects.body:
## Project Overview

In the VIRCL (Virtualization in the Cloud) module, we deployed and compared two industry-standard Type 1 hypervisors, **Proxmox VE** and **VMware ESXi**, on real HP server hardware in the school server room. Starting from bare-metal installation via ILO remote management, we covered the full lifecycle of virtual machines: creation via GUI and CLI, hardware configuration, cloning, snapshots, templates, backups, storage migration, and live hypervisor migration. Our specialisation topic is **High Availability (HA)**.

## Team

- Würth Eric
- Simon Max
- Kugener Sven

## Hypervisors Used

- **Proxmox VE**: open-source Linux-based hypervisor (KVM + LXC), free to use, managed via a web UI and command line. Installed on HP09.
- **VMware ESXi**: industry-leading commercial Type 1 hypervisor by Broadcom, managed via the vSphere Client and vCenter Server Appliance (VCSA). Installed on HP11/HP12.

## What We Implemented

- **Hypervisor Installation**: Remote deployment via ILO5 HTML5 console; network configuration (static IP, gateway, DNS)
- **VM Creation (GUI & CLI)**: Creating VMs through the web interface and via `qm create` (Proxmox) / `vmkfstools` + `vim-cmd` (ESXi)
- **OS Installation**: Ubuntu 24.04 LTS (Linux server) and Windows 10/11 within VMs on both hypervisors
- **Hardware Changes**: Adding/removing CPU cores, RAM, hard disks and NICs; live hot-plug of CPU/RAM where supported
- **Clone / Duplicate**: Cloning VMs via GUI (Proxmox right-click Clone; vSphere Clone wizard) and by manually copying .vmdk/.vmx files on ESXi
- **Export**: Exporting VMs as OVF/OVA (ESXi) and vzdump archives (Proxmox)
- **Hypervisor Config Backup**: `tar czf proxmox-config-backup.tar.gz /etc/pve/` on Proxmox; `vim-cmd hostsvc/firmware/backup_config` on ESXi
- **VM Backup**: Built-in scheduled backup jobs (Proxmox Datacenter → Backup); ghettoVCB script-based backup on ESXi Free
- **Snapshots**: Create / rollback / delete snapshots on both platforms
- **VM Templates**: Convert to template (Proxmox right-click; ESXi Template menu); manual VMDK clone + VMX edit workaround on ESXi Free
- **Remote Storage (CLOIF2 NAS)**: Connected TrueNAS via NFS (Proxmox) and iSCSI (ESXi); used as shared datastore for VM files
- **Storage Migration**: Live move of VM disks from local storage to NFS/iSCSI datastore while VM is running
- **Hypervisor Migration (vMotion / Proxmox Migrate)**: Live migration of running VMs between two hypervisor nodes using shared iSCSI storage
- **User & Permission Management**: Proxmox datacenter users + roles; vCenter SSO users, custom roles, and ACL propagation
- **Patching**: ESXi compliance check via vSphere Lifecycle Manager; host reported Compliant against Critical Host Patches baseline
- **High Availability (Specialisation)**: vSphere HA cluster with two ESXi hosts, shared iSCSI storage, heartbeat datastores, admission control and failure response policies configured

projects.title: TrueNAS NAS Server
projects.subtitle: CLOIF2: Cloud Infrastructure
projects.summary: Setup and configuration of a TrueNAS Community Edition NAS server on real server hardware, CLOIF2 group project
projects.body:
## Project Overview

In the CLOIF2 (Cloud Infrastructure) module, our group of three set up and fully configured a TrueNAS Community Edition NAS server on real enterprise server hardware. Starting from bare metal, we covered everything from RAID controller staging, OS installation, and network configuration through to user management, dataset creation, and client connectivity from both Windows and Linux.

## Group

- Würth Eric
- Simon Max
- Kugener Sven

## Hardware

We worked on an **Intel SR2600URBRPR**: a 2U rack-mounted server with the following specs:

- **CPU**: 2× Intel Xeon X5650
- **RAM**: 8× 8 GB (64 GB total)
- **Native HDD (SATA)**: 2× 160 GB
- **RAID HDD (SAS)**: 3× 146 GB via Areca RAID controller with backup battery

## Software

**TrueNAS Community Edition** (formerly TrueNAS SCALE) is an open-source, Debian-based NAS OS using the ZFS file system, developed by iXsystems. Free to use with the same codebase as the enterprise edition.

## What We Configured

- **RAID Staging**: Accessed the Areca RAID controller web interface to prepare the hardware RAID array before OS installation
- **OS Installation**: Installed TrueNAS Community Edition on the server
- **Network Configuration**: Set a static IP, configured hostname, gateway, and DNS via the TrueNAS console and web UI
- **Storage Pools**: Created both a software RAID pool (Mirror) and a hardware RAID pool (Stripe) using ZFS
- **Users & Permissions**: Created SMB-enabled users and set ACL-based permissions on datasets
- **File Sharing**: Connected to the NAS share from a Windows client (File Explorer / SMB) and from a Linux client (Nautilus / smb://)
- **iSCSI vs NFS/SMB**: Studied and documented the differences between block-level (iSCSI) and file-level (NFS/SMB) storage protocols

projects.title: Spinning
projects.subtitle: LGK: Relais pour la Vie
projects.summary: Class-wide project for Relais pour la Vie at LGK, built the online leaderboard
projects.body: ## Project Overview Spinning was a class-wide project organized for **Relais pour la Vie** at our school (LGK). Instead of one big group working on everything together, every team in the class took ownership of a different part of the overall system. My part was building the **online leaderboard** that displayed live results during the event. ## My Role - **Online Leaderboard**: designed and built the live leaderboard with SvelteKit ## Technology Stack ### Frontend - **SvelteKit**: used to build and serve the live leaderboard interface ## Working Across Teams Because the project was split between several teams, each working on its own module, the biggest lesson wasn't technical it was about **dividing the work**. Staying within your own area worked well, but as soon as a topic crossed into someone else's scope, it had to be actively communicated rather than decided alone. A good example was **anonymizing student data**: this touched three different teams at once (Frontend, Frontend Admin and Database), so all of us had to sit down together and agree on a shared approach before anyone could keep building.

externals.meta: Former BTS CLC student, Project Management
externals.text: Jamey, a former BTS CLC student, showed us how project management actually works in the real world: how large companies handle big budgets, deadlines, and stakeholders on real projects, beyond what we see in the theoretical course material.

externals.name: Arnaud Charlier
externals.meta: ARHS Group, Luxembourg: Introduction to AWS
externals.text: Arnaud, from ARHS Group here in Luxembourg, spent a full week introducing us to AWS. Since we mostly work with Azure in class, it was valuable to see a different cloud provider and get a broader perspective on the cloud landscape.

externals.name: Xavier Nix
externals.text: Xavier taught us PowerShell and PS scripting. What made it interesting was learning the topic from a real expert instead of a regular teacher, and spending a whole week on the same subject, which let us go much deeper into the details and made it stick a lot better.

externals.name: Noah Gallo & Clara Morgante
externals.text: Noah and Clara from Devoteam Luxembourg ran a French language mock interview with us, Noah as the IT expert and Clara on the HR side. It was a realistic look at how a technical interview is actually structured and judged from both sides of the table.

externals.name: ARHS Group Visit
externals.text: We visited ARHS Group again for a recap of AWS re:Invent, where they walked us through a wide range of AWS IT solutions and tools that were announced or highlighted at the conference.
